author: BBC News
description:
A senior US soldier has been arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia.

The 41-year-old officer was detained on Tuesday. Counter-terrorism police said the man had been arrested under national security laws relating to obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

The BBC understands the soldier is based at Imjin Barracks in Gloucestershire, which is headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, a strategic operational base for the alliance.

The director of the FBI director Kash Patel said in a statement: "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies."

He added: "While this investigation is continuing, I want to send a clear message – this FBI has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners."

Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, from Counte
title: Senior US soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested at Nato base in UK | BBC News

description:
Today, David Walliams has been named as the ‘well-known celebrity’ who was fighting in the courts to block the publication of serious allegations against him of sexual misconduct.

The comedian and author is accused of preying on girls as young as 15. In allegations published by the Guardian and ITN, multiple women accuse Walliams of using his celebrity status to prey on them for sexual purposes. In a letter to the journalists investigating the claims, Walliams strongly denied all allegations, saying: "I am not a sexual predator." But he acknowledged that "at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people”.

Adam is joined by Dominic Casciani, home and legal affairs correspondent and Noor Nanji, culture and royal correspondent to unpack what’s been happening.

WARNING: This video includes refrences to sexual violence, which may be disturbing to some viewers. 

A BBC investigation has revealed new evidence that powerful figures in the fashion world, including modelling agencies and scouts, helped Jeffrey Epstein gain access to young women after his conviction for sex offences. The US authorities' release of the Epstein files beginning last year has led to growing calls for Epstein's associates and enablers to be brought to account. 

Several Democrat lawmakers have promised to take action against people accused of involvement in Epstein's crimes. And with the party set to take control of the House and Senate, they will have more power to do so. 

Earlier this year, President Donald Trump dismissed questions about Epstein, saying it was "time for the country to get onto something else". Mr Trump's name appeared more than 6,000 times in documents related to Epstein. He has consistently denied any wrongdoing.

You can watch the full documentary

author: BBC News
description:
Torrential rain has reportedly flooded more than 70,000 tents across Gaza, leaving four dead and many Palestinians without a dry place to sleep.
 
Three children and one woman were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in central Gaza following heavy rain, the Hamas-run health ministry says.
 
The Civil Defence service, which operates under the Hamas-run interior ministry, said the "humanitarian tragedy" should prompt urgent action by international organisations to provide safe shelters for displaced people and move tents away from sandy areas, slopes and locations at risk of collapse.
 
UN agencies have called on Israeli authorities to allow in the specialist equipment and materials required to improve living conditions for displaced families.
 
The BBC spoke to many residents who say the major storms have compounded their misery.

author: BBC News
description:
More than a dozen US Air Force aircraft have left a second airbase in Britain weeks after the US withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford over a suspected Iran-linked security incident.
 
The latest plane to leave, a Boeing Stratotanker KC-135 refuelling aircraft, flew from RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk on Tuesday afternoon and headed towards Germany.
 
The Wall Street Journal reported that the departures have been in response to a further threat from Iran but the BBC has not independently verified that claim.
 
Downing Street has insisted British air bases are safe and that their security is a "top priority".

author: BBC News
description:
Warning: Distressing content

David Walliams has been named as the celebrity who tried to block publication of sexual misconduct allegations.

ITV News and the Guardian have reported allegations the comedian and author groomed fans as young as 15 and harassed women in the workplace over a number of years.

Walliams has denied all allegations but acknowledged "at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with".

He added: “I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

He had asked the High Court to block the publication of the investigation, with his lawyers arguing if the allegations were made public he would likely kill himself.

The court refused the request, saying the risks could be mitigated and that it was not the court's responsibility to protect his wellbeing.

title: David Walliams loses court bid to block publication of sexual misconduct allegations | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
Jemima Goldsmith, the ex-girlfriend of Russell Brand, has accused him of "violence, coercive control and abuse" while the two were together.
 
Goldsmith, who dated the disgraced entertainer for roughly a year around 2014, alleged she "had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident" but chose not to press charges.
 
In a lengthy statement on social media, the 52-year-old said she was "in awe of the courageous women who came forward at Brand's trial" and was "glad and relieved" he had "finally faced justice".
 
Brand, 51, was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison earlier on Monday after being convicted of rape and sexual assault.
